description: NaBaFeF₆ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pna2₁ space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 7-coordinate geometry to seven F atoms. There are a spread of Na-F bond distances ranging from 2.34-2.70 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight F atoms. There are a spread of Na-F bond distances ranging from 2.35-2.83 Å. There are two inequivalent Ba sites. In the first Ba site, Ba is bonded in a 10-coordinate geometry to ten F atoms. There are a spread of Ba-F bond distances ranging from 2.66-3.26 Å. In the second Ba site, Ba is bonded in a 10-coordinate geometry to ten F atoms. There are a spread of Ba-F bond distances ranging from 2.63-3.28 Å. There are two inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded in an octahedral geometry to six F atoms. There are a spread of Fe-F bond distances ranging from 1.94-1.98 Å. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded in an octahedral geometry to six F atoms. There are a spread of Fe-F bond distances ranging from 1.93-1.99 Å. There are twelve inequivalent F sites. In the first F site, F is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, two Ba, and one Fe atom. In the second F site, F is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, two equivalent Ba, and one Fe atom. In the third F site, F is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Ba, and one Fe atom. In the fourth F site, F is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, two Ba, and one Fe atom. In the fifth F site, F is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, two Ba, and one Fe atom. In the sixth F site, F is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, two equivalent Ba, and one Fe atom. In the seventh F site, F is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Ba, and one Fe atom. In the eighth F site, F is bonded to two Na, one Ba, and one Fe atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing FBaNa₂Fe trigonal pyramids. In the ninth F site, F is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, two Ba, and one Fe atom. In the tenth F site, F is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to two Ba and one Fe atom. In the eleventh F site, F is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, two Ba, and one Fe atom. In the twelfth F site, F is bonded to two Na, one Ba, and one Fe atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing FBaNa₂Fe trigonal pyramids.
